Not sure if this is a good place to post this but I just feel like unloading some mental baggage and I would rather do it on Voat than some dusty old blog that nobody will read.

So many changes are happening and I can't stop the wheels from spinning in my head. One of my best friends, whom I also work with, just put in his 2 weeks notice. I have other friends here but he is the only one I've actually bonded with. Everyone else is more of an acquaintance.

When he talked to our boss, who is also the owner, the boss said he recognizes that this company isn't a final destination. It's a "stepping stone". I've been working here for roughly 6 years and now more than ever I feel an intense urge to move on. Especially with the stepping stone analogy. I feel like I've set up camp on a stepping stone in the middle of a river and I'm convincing myself that this is as good a campsite as any. Convincing myself that I'm comfortable here.

To put it in perspective, my current employer doesn't offer any benefits whatsoever, I recently got a raise but the owner said were at the highest our payroll has ever been and he doesn't see the budget getting any looser. We have hit a plateau in terms of growth and development and without expanding, the company will either go under or just live on in obscurity at the same level it's at. My boss seems content or oblivious to that.

I can't shake the feeling that I'm on board the titanic and we're slowly approaching an iceberg.

The company is almost totally reliant on one machine that hasn't undergone any regular maintenance and if it breaks down, the entire company is fucked.

I'm thinking about getting a CDL but this decision is entirely financially motivated. I am in no way interested in the shipping industry, and even though I'd be getting paid way more than I am now, I feel like it would be the final nail in the coffin of anything dreams or aspirations I still cling to.

The philosophical side of my brain says "who gives a shit? Driving a truck is no different than any other job. Everyone does what they do to get by. Money I'd make by becoming an animator or writer or musician would spend the same way. It's all the same and happiness is subjective." but I still romanticize delusions of grandeur, even if they keep becoming increasingly unrealistic.

Sorry guys. I'm a mess of a human being.

Tldr; I'm stuck at a crossroads desperately trying to convince myself that it's an acceptable place to stay because I'm too much of a pussy to be an adult.

I found out the hard way that staying in one place at the same level, for too long, ends up with you having to stay there forever (or until the company goes belly up)

Move on while you can, driving a truck in successful company is better than driving one in a bankrupt company.

And it seems you have dreams

Money I'd make by becoming an animator or writer or musician would spend the same way. It's all the same and happiness is subjective."

Aim for them, you will never know if you don't try. Get on the web, find some classes, advice, hell even post something here. Don't try to be an adult, try to do what you enjoy.

Newish player here but familiar with WoT. So I've become frustrated with Battleship game play, it mainly goes like this...

1) Start game 2) Full speed ahead, choose direction to go 3) Watch the turrets slowly turn...purdy! 4) Get volleyed out of the game by the 2 carrier torp bombers on the enemy team 5) Return to port

Getting a bit shit now....

Couple of suggetions:

  1. Beginning tier BB's are absolutely horrible, and there is no sense of teamwork. I recommend either playing with friends, use free xp from other ships to get through them quickly, but occasionally play a few games to get used to the slow rudder shift and long lead times.

  2. Mid tier, you start getting the health to survive multiple torps. Remember to save your repair until you know, that all squads have dropped torps. Look at the opponents carriers and assume they have all torp squads (tier 4, 2 per, t5, 3 per etc etc). After playing a bit you'll soon know just by looking how many torp planes that carrer can have.

  3. Encourage teamwork, if no one calls out directions, speak up. Also ask for air cover, a lot of USN CL's don't mind providing escorts as they start getting great AA cover.

  4. IJN's start getting good range at T5 with the Kongo. like 22K away with scout plane.

  5. Save your shots for the good angle to get citadels. Dispersion rate sucks, we all know this, Wargaming knows this, and they have no plans to change. If you have a hard time figuring out how much to lead, fire a test shot, then readjust for your next volley.
